key_insight: ESMFold folds a beta hairpin via two computational stages: early transformer blocks initialize pairwise biochemical signals (residue identity and charge flow) from sequence representations, and later blocks consolidate those signals into the final structural predictions.
problem_solved: Explains how internal computations of a state‑of‑the‑art protein folding model generate and transform biochemical signals to produce 3D structure, improving interpretability of model mechanisms.
method: Trace folding of a prototypical motif (beta hairpin) through ESMFold’s transformer layers.
Apply counterfactual interventions on model latents to test causal roles of representations (e.g., altering sequence-derived features and observing pairwise representation changes).
Layer‑wise analysis to identify two-stage computation: initialization of pairwise biochemical features in early blocks and subsequent refinement/consolidation in later blocks.
impact: Clarifies internal mechanisms of large protein folding models, enabling practitioners to better diagnose, trust, and guide model design (e.g., targeted interventions, architecture choices, or incorporating biochemical priors).
visual_elements: Two‑stage schematic: early blocks (sequence → biochemical pair signals) vs. later blocks (refinement → 3D fold).
Flow diagram showing information flow: amino acid sequence → sequence embeddings → pairwise representations → predicted structure.
Heatmap or matrix visual of pairwise biochemical signals (charge/identity) evolving across layers.
Counterfactual intervention cartoon: altering a latent and showing change/no‑change in downstream pair signals and final structure.
paper_title: Mechanisms of AI Protein Folding in ESMFold
paper_authors: Kevin Lu, Jannik Brinkmann, Stefan Huber, Aaron Mueller, Yonatan Belinkov
